finding.claim: Ruby Integers in 2^62..2^63-1 returned from user functions are silently converted to REAL on 64-bit platforms, losing precision (1024-wide collapse).
finding.source: Ruby function (define_function or aggregate finalize) returns a Bignum in 2^62..2^63-1, e.g. a 63-bit hash or ID computed from attacker input.
finding.sink: sqlite3_result_double at database.c:521 (via set_sqlite3_func_result, also reached from aggregator.c:164).

trace.note: case T_BIGNUM entered in set_sqlite3_func_result
int64 conversion guarded by #if SIZEOF_LONG < 8; compiled out on LP64 (Linux/macOS)
control falls through to case T_FLOAT
sqlite3_result_double(ctx, NUM2DBL(result)) stores a lossy REAL
contrast: bind path uses bignum_to_int64 unconditionally, so binds are exact

finding.guards_checked: Bind path (statement.c:285-291) is exact; the defect is only on the result path. No range check before the double conversion.

finding.claim: Authorizer, trace, busy-handler and collation callbacks call Ruby without rb_protect; a raising callback longjmps through SQLite internals with its mutex held.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled SQL text supplies table/column names passed as authorizer args (database.c:733-737); attacker-stored values drive collation comparisons. Precondition: the application callback raises on such input.
finding.sink: rb_funcall inside SQLite callbacks (database.c:738 authorizer, 328 trace, 365 busy handler, 839 collation compare, 841 NUM2INT).

trace.note: sqlite3_prepare_v2 runs with the db mutex held
authorizer args a..d built from attacker SQL identifiers
rb_funcall(authorizer, call) with no rb_protect; exception longjmps
set_authorizer registers rb_sqlite3_auth without a protective wrapper

finding.guards_checked: Scalar functions (database.c:554-588) and aggregator step/finalize (aggregator.c:48-50) use rb_protect; these four callbacks do not. No protection on the path.

finding.claim: step re-raises the ambient $! after a successful sqlite3_step when called inside a rescue or ensure clause, discarding the row and clearing $!.
finding.source: Application calls Statement#step (or execute) while an exception is being handled or unwound.
finding.sink: rb_exc_raise at statement.c:149 with rb_set_errinfo(Qnil) at statement.c:148.

trace.note: sqlite3_step returns SQLITE_ROW or DONE successfully
rb_errinfo() returns $!, non-nil inside rescue/ensure
rb_set_errinfo(Qnil) clears $!
rb_exc_raise re-raises the unrelated in-flight exception

finding.guards_checked: None: the check does not distinguish errinfo set by a user callback from ambient $!. Not executed; based on Ruby errinfo semantics.

finding.claim: Aggregate finalize result conversion runs outside rb_protect; an unsupported return type longjmps and skips instance destruction, leaking one instance per failing query.
finding.source: Aggregate finalize returns a type set_sqlite3_func_result rejects (Array, Hash, Symbol). Whether attacker data reaches that return depends on the application.
finding.sink: set_sqlite3_func_result raise at database.c:543-544, reached from aggregator.c:164; instance retained in -instances.

trace.note: finalize protected call returns result
set_sqlite3_func_result called unprotected
rb_sqlite3_aggregate_instance_destroy skipped on longjmp
instance pushed into -instances
instances pinned by GC marking, so they are never freed

finding.guards_checked: rb_protect covers finalize itself but not the result conversion that follows.

finding.claim: statement_timeout ignores the configured milliseconds; the deadline is set at the first progress tick, so queries over about 2000 VM opcodes are interrupted regardless of the value.
finding.source: Application sets db.statement_timeout to any non-zero value.

trace.note: stmt_timeout stored but never read
first tick sets stmt_deadline = now
later tick with time after deadline returns 1 (interrupt)
deadline cleared only in prepare, not in reset!, so reused statements can be interrupted early

finding.guards_checked: None relevant. Over-restriction, not a bypass.

finding.claim: statement_timeout= lacks REQUIRE_OPEN_DB, so sqlite3_progress_handler may be called with a NULL db on a closed connection.
finding.source: Application code calls statement_timeout= on a closed Database.
finding.sink: sqlite3_progress_handler(ctx->db, ...) at database.c:445 with ctx->db NULL.

trace.note: set_statement_timeout has no open-database check
progress handler registered with NULL db
contrast: set_busy_timeout uses REQUIRE_OPEN_DB

finding.guards_checked: Bundled SQLite source is not in this tree, so whether sqlite3_progress_handler NULL-checks its argument is unverified.

finding.claim: READONLY (and DISCARDED) connection flags are never cleared on reopen, so a writable reopened connection is treated as read-only at fork and gets an ordinary close that the code's own comment says can corrupt the database.
finding.source: Application reopens the same Database object read-write after a read-only open, then forks.
finding.sink: close_or_discard_db ordinary sqlite3_close_v2 at database.c:65-68 in the child process.

trace.note: READONLY flag set on read-only open, never cleared
REQUIRE_CLOSED_DB permits reopening the same object
is_readonly read from sticky flag
owner check bypassed for readonly, so ordinary close on inherited handle

finding.guards_checked: Fork ownership check (database.c:65) is bypassed by the sticky flag. Requires reopen plus fork, so low likelihood; whether the Ruby layer exposes reopen is not visible here.
